evidence.title: An Exploration-Exploitation Approach to Anti-lock Brake Systems
evidence.abstract: Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) is a mandatory active safety feature on road vehicles with analogous systems for aircraft and locomotives. This feature aims to prevent locking of the wheels when braking and to improve the handling performance, as well as reduce stopping distance of the vehicle. Estimation uncertainties in the vehicle state and environment (road surface) are often neglected or handled separately from the ABS controller, leading to sub-optimal braking. In this paper, a Dual Control for Exploration-Exploitation (DCEE) approach is taken toward the ABS problem which achieves both accurate state (and environment) estimation and superior braking performance. Compared with popular Extremum Seeking methods, improvements of up to $15\%$ and $8.5\%$ are shown in stopping time and stopping distance, respectively. A Regularized Particle Filter with Markov Chain Monte Carlo step is used to estimate vehicle states and parameters of the Magic Formula tyre model that includes the peak friction coefficient for the environment. The effectiveness of the DCEE approach is demonstrated across a range of driving scenarios such as low and high speeds; snow, wet and dry roads and changing road surfaces.

evidence.title: Possible evolution of the pulsar braking index from larger than three to about one
evidence.abstract: The coupled evolution of pulsar rotation and inclination angle in the wind braking model is calculated. The oblique pulsar tends to align. The pulsar alignment will affect its spin-down behavior. As a pulsar evolves from the magneto-dipole radiation dominated case to the particle wind dominated case, the braking index will first increase and then decrease. In the early time, the braking index may be larger than 3. And during the following long time, the braking index will be always smaller than 3. The minimum braking index is about one. This can explain the existence of high braking index larger than 3, and low braking index of pulsars simultaneously. The pulsar braking index is expected to evolve from larger than three to about one. A general trend is that the pulsar braking index will evolve from the Crab-like case to the Vela-like case.

evidence.title: On the braking index evolution of PSR B0540-69: wind braking of pulsars
evidence.abstract: The pulsar PSR B0540-69 has both a braking index measurement and spin-down state change. After its spin-down state change, it shows an increasing braking index with time. Previously, it is pointed out that the spin-down state change may be caused by an enhanced particle wind. The prediction is that its braking index will be smaller in the high spin-down state. The current measured braking index is approaching the previous prediction. The transient variation of braking index may be due to a small varying part of the particle density. The braking index evolution of PSR B0540-69 is found to be in an exponential form. Its braking index is expected to approach some steady value. Future braking index measurement may make clear the physics for the braking index evolution. It may also help to make test the particle acceleration mechanism in the pulsar magnetosphere. Finally, a phenomenological treatment of the wind braking model is presented in the appendix. It can simplify the applications of wind braking model to pulsar braking index, intermittent pulsars and PSR B0540-69.

evidence.title: Model-based Fault Detection and Diagnosis of the Anti-lock Braking System
evidence.abstract: The ABS is one of the latest improvements to the braking system, which prevent the vehicle’s brakes from locking up and skidding during hard stops on icy or wet roads. ABS controllers are characterized by robust adaptive behaviour with respect to highly uncertain tyre characteristics and fast changing road surface properties. Performance improvement is typically sought in the areas of stability, steerability and stopping distance. In this paper, a non-linear mathematical model of the ABS is developed and ABS system is modelled using Simulink and some of the results are displayed which demonstrate the potential of the proposed model-based prognostics approach

evidence.title: An ABS control logic based on wheel force measurement
evidence.abstract: The paper presents an anti-lock braking system (ABS) control logic based on the measurement of the longitudinal forces at the hub bearings. The availability of force information allows to design a logic that does not rely on the estimation of the tyre-road friction coefficient, since it continuously tries to exploit the maximum longitudinal tyre force. The logic is designed by means of computer simulation and then tested on a specific hardware in the loop test bench: the experimental results confirm that measured wheel force can lead to a significant improvement of the ABS performances in terms of stopping distance also in the presence of road with variable friction coefficien

mechanism_map.mechanism: Dual Control for Exploration-Exploitation (DCEE) with a Regularized Particle Filter plus Markov Chain Monte Carlo step that jointly estimates vehicle states and road-surface (environment) parameters, folding estimation directly into the ABS controller instead of keeping it separate.
mechanism_map.intervention: Reflash/reprogram the 2019 Silverado 1500's ABS/ESC ECU to run the DCEE estimator, fusing wheel-speed, yaw-rate, steering, and engine/PCM data (the check-engine channel) so that vehicle state and peak friction coefficient are estimated online and consumed by the brake-control loop, eliminating the detached estimation path that sets the fault state.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Braking ability is restored and the ABS, ESC, and check engine warnings clear, because the controller no longer operates on neglected/mismatched state and environment estimates that trigger degraded-mode operation and sub-optimal braking.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Reproduce the fault in the vehicle, then flash the DCEE estimator and drive the same low-speed driveway maneuver plus a documented stopping-distance run; the mechanism is falsified if any of the three warnings re-illuminates or if stopping distance/time fails to return to the pre-fault baseline.
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: Estimation uncertainties in the vehicle state and environment (road surface) are often neglected or handled separately from the ABS controller, leading to sub-optimal braking.

candidates.mechanism: Brake commands are made dual-purpose: they regulate wheel slip toward the peak of the tyre-friction curve while deliberately probing the vehicle/road system so estimation uncertainty in vehicle state and road surface is reduced online rather than neglected; a Regularized Particle Filter with an MCMC step estimates vehicle states and Magic Formula tyre parameters including peak friction coefficient, and the ABS/ESC controller exploits those estimates to prevent wheel lock and preserve braking/handling.
candidates.intervention: Instantiate the demonstrated Dual Control for Exploration-Exploitation (DCEE) ABS approach in the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 braking controller: add the Regularized Particle Filter with MCMC step for state/environment estimation, including peak friction coefficient, and modify brake-pressure/ESC commands to include an exploration component whose size is driven by estimate uncertainty; use the same estimator as a consistency check for ABS/ESC/check-engine fault logic so residual sensor/actuator faults are separated from road-surface uncertainty.

evidence_bundle.mechanism_source_span: In this paper, a Dual Control for Exploration-Exploitation (DCEE) approach is taken toward the ABS problem which achieves both accurate state (and environment) estimation and superior braking performance. Compared with popular Extremum Seeking methods, improvements of up to $15\%$ and $8.5\%$ are shown in stopping time and stopping distance, respectively. A Regularized Particle Filter with Markov Chain Monte Carlo step is used to estimate vehicle states and parameters of the Magic Formula tyre model that includes the peak friction coefficient for the environment.

constraint_set.problem_constraint: braking ability must be restored and ABS, ESC, and check engine warnings must be resolved
constraint_set.boundary_conditions: Functional brake actuators and sensors; speeds and surfaces within the demonstrated envelope (low/high speed; snow, wet, dry, changing roads); sufficient time/data for estimator convergence before hard braking; not valid as a standalone repair for hardware faults.

candidates.predicted_effect: For braking loss attributable to estimation/control uncertainty, stopping time and stopping distance improve toward the demonstrated gains (up to 15% and 8.5% versus Extremum Seeking), wheel-lock events decrease, and the ABS/ESC/check-engine warning state is expected to clear only after the estimator converges and sensor/actuator consistency is verified.
known_failure_modes: exploration probing may excite brake/driveline vibration or interfere with ESC stability
particle degeneracy or poor MCMC mixing during abrupt surface changes can misestimate peak friction
faulty wheel-speed, pressure, or yaw sensors make the filter unreliable
the software mechanism will not restore braking or clear warnings if the root cause is a mechanical/electrical brake fault
candidates.novel_design_variable: uncertainty-weighted exploration amplitude in the brake-pressure command.
candidates.testable_prediction: On a 2019 Silverado 1500 with verified functional brake hardware, during low- and high-speed braking on snow, wet, dry, and changing road surfaces, the DCEE-tuned controller will reduce stopping time and stopping distance relative to an Extremum-Seeking ABS calibration while keeping wheel slip below the lock threshold; absence of improvement or persistent estimates inconsistent with measured wheel speeds falsifies the transfer.

custody_records.raw_content: Anti-lock Brake System (ABS) is a mandatory active safety feature on road vehicles with analogous systems for aircraft and locomotives. This feature aims to prevent locking of the wheels when braking and to improve the handling performance, as well as reduce stopping distance of the vehicle. Estimation uncertainties in the vehicle state and environment (road surface) are often neglected or handled separately from the ABS controller, leading to sub-optimal braking. In this paper, a Dual Control for Exploration-Exploitation (DCEE) approach is taken toward the ABS problem which achieves both accurate state (and environment) estimation and superior braking performance. Compared with popular Extremum Seeking methods, improvements of up to $15\%$ and $8.5\%$ are shown in stopping time and stopping distance, respectively. A Regularized Particle Filter with Markov Chain Monte Carlo step is used to estimate vehicle states and parameters of the Magic Formula tyre model that includes the peak friction coefficient for the environment. The effectiveness of the DCEE approach is demonstrated across a range of driving scenarios such as low and high speeds; snow, wet and dry roads and changing road surfaces.

custody_records.raw_content: The coupled evolution of pulsar rotation and inclination angle in the wind braking model is calculated. The oblique pulsar tends to align. The pulsar alignment will affect its spin-down behavior. As a pulsar evolves from the magneto-dipole radiation dominated case to the particle wind dominated case, the braking index will first increase and then decrease. In the early time, the braking index may be larger than 3. And during the following long time, the braking index will be always smaller than 3. The minimum braking index is about one. This can explain the existence of high braking index larger than 3, and low braking index of pulsars simultaneously. The pulsar braking index is expected to evolve from larger than three to about one. A general trend is that the pulsar braking index will evolve from the Crab-like case to the Vela-like case.

custody_records.raw_content: The pulsar PSR B0540-69 has both a braking index measurement and spin-down state change. After its spin-down state change, it shows an increasing braking index with time. Previously, it is pointed out that the spin-down state change may be caused by an enhanced particle wind. The prediction is that its braking index will be smaller in the high spin-down state. The current measured braking index is approaching the previous prediction. The transient variation of braking index may be due to a small varying part of the particle density. The braking index evolution of PSR B0540-69 is found to be in an exponential form. Its braking index is expected to approach some steady value. Future braking index measurement may make clear the physics for the braking index evolution. It may also help to make test the particle acceleration mechanism in the pulsar magnetosphere. Finally, a phenomenological treatment of the wind braking model is presented in the appendix. It can simplify the applications of wind braking model to pulsar braking index, intermittent pulsars and PSR B0540-69.

ABS controllers are characterized by robust adaptive behaviour with respect to highly uncertain tyre characteristics and fast changing road surface properties. Performance improvement is typically sought in the areas of stability, steerability and stopping distance. In this paper, a non-linear mathematical model of the ABS is developed and ABS system is modelled using Simulink and some of the results are displayed which demonstrate the potential of the proposed model-based prognostics approach
